title: Attenuated burst synthesis notebook - Rylan
content:
Purpose
- Quick personal lab notes for a set of microbenchmarks exploring a "mesh"-style shaping layer we introduced last sprint. Goal: quantify how a short randomized splay on admission (0-100ms) + soft attenuation (drop probability scaling with queue depth) affects p99 tail during 1:1 burst loads.

Test rig and baseline
- Single-node dedicated GPU (A10G emulation), 1 model instance pinned.
- Model: open-gpt-small-8bit (fp16->int8 quant), kv-cache enabled.
- Serving runtime: local branch mesh-splay-v2 (w/ continuous batching), gRPC client harness.
- Client: synthetic Poisson+burst generator, fixed-seed, 10k requests per run.
- Request mix: 70% short (20 tokens), 30% medium (120 tokens).
- Concurrency cap: 256 outstanding requests.
- Baseline (no splay, no attenuation) for reference.

Parameters varied
- splay_ms: {0, 10, 30, 60, 100}  (random uniform up to value)
- soft_drop_curve: linear scaling drop_prob = min(0.5, alpha*(queue_depth / cap)), alpha in {0.5, 1.0, 2.0}
- prefill_hint: enabled/disabled (prefill simulates KV cache priming for repeated prefixes)
- batch_window_ms: fixed 8ms for these runs

What I measured
- p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency (client-observed)
- model-step latency (server-side per-token)
- queue_depth distribution samples (percentiles)
- observed qps and GPU utilization
- percent requests dropped by soft_drop layer (should be small)

Selected run results (abridged)
- Baseline (splay=0, alpha=0): p50=45ms p95=220ms p99=740ms qps=420 gpu_util=72%

- splay=10ms, alpha=0.5, prefill=on: p50=48ms p95=165ms p99=310ms qps=398 gpu_util=68% drop=0.6%
- splay=30ms, alpha=1.0, prefill=on: p50=52ms p95=140ms p99=240ms qps=385 gpu_util=64% drop=1.7%
- splay=60ms, alpha=2.0, prefill=on: p50=61ms p95=190ms p99=420ms qps=352 gpu_util=55% drop=4.4%
- splay=100ms, alpha=2.0, prefill=off: p50=68ms p95=260ms p99=960ms qps=300 gpu_util=46% drop=3.9%

Observations and quick interpretation
1) Small randomized splay (10-30ms) + light attenuation (alpha<=1) reduced p99 by ~2-3x vs baseline while only modestly lowering throughput (5-10%). Intuition: the splay de-synchronizes simultaneous arrivals causing fewer huge contiguous batches that overload the runtime and force long queueing.
2) Heavier attenuation (alpha=2.0) or larger splay (60-100ms) shifted the system into an underutilized regime: p50 increases and p99 sometimes worsens (esp when prefill=cold). Too much randomization effectively converts burst capacity into idle time.
3) Prefill (KV cache priming) materially interacts — when prefill=on the beneficial region of splay widens and optimal alpha is higher. Likely because primed KV reduces per-request model-step time and smooths batching.
4) Drop rates under sensible configs stayed <2% and correlated with tail improvements. These are likely acceptable for low-priority background embedding workloads but need product review for latency-sensitive chat routes.

Notes on telemetry artifacts
- I grabbed flamegraphs for a 30s window at splay=30ms/alpha=1: most of increased p99 in baseline maps to long queueing inside admission. With splay the time is distributed.
- GPU utilization track shows clear smoothing: baseline had peaked bursts to 98% then idle; splay runs kept steady ~60-75%.

Actionable next experiments
- Try adaptive splay: increase splay when instantaneous queue_depth > thresh, otherwise minimal. Hypothesis: keeps latency low when quiet and de-syncs when bursting.
- Evaluate impact on multi-tenant noisy neighbors: run synthetic cross-tenant mix to see if attenuation helps tenant isolation.
- Run with variable batch_window_ms (4ms, 12ms) — there may be interaction with splay that changes optimal window.
- Longer runs (1M requests) to validate low-frequency tail events.

Open questions and TODOs
- What's acceptable drop policy for customer-facing chat by product (CC to Mira/Product)?
- Tune threshold for adaptive splay and build a microcontroller in serving-runtime for rollout toggles.
- Add integration test that reproduces p99 regression if splay disabled (linked PR as temporary PoC).

Quick checklist for next session
- [ ] Implement adaptive-splay prototype in mesh-splay-v2 branch
- [ ] Run cross-tenant experiment with 3 tenants (one noisy, two steady)
- [ ] Add histogram sampling to client harness for more stable p99 estimates
- [ ] Draft short note for product about drop vs tail tradeoff (cc: Mira)

Raw excerpt of one run latency histogram (splay=30ms, alpha=1.0, prefill=on)
- bucket(ms): count
- 0-50: 6200
- 50-100: 2400
- 100-200: 900
- 200-500: 350
- 500-1000: 120
- >1000: 30

Sign-off
- Rylan (quick personal notes). Will tidy into a formal experiment doc if any of the adaptive-splay prototypes show consistent wins in multi-tenant tests.
